READING THE MAP

A research register,
not a confirmed attack count.

112 records: the 84 baseline records, 27 new event additions and one unidentified object under Alert / other. Eight aggregate/context records remain separate.

The baseline retains its original discoveries, clusters, alerts and related-object records. The update adds distinct dated discoveries even when the original flight date or airframe identity is unknown. The unidentified object is not a confirmed drone. Supplementary daily bulletins and precautionary alerts remain in the research download and are excluded from this map. Aggregate totals are never added to the map count.

Positions are approximate

The file does not supply verified incident coordinates. Markers are editorial anchors at the named locality, region or offshore area. A regional marker does not identify a crash site, flight path, jurisdiction boundary or precise offshore position. Every record is drawn individually, with a minimum visible size at every zoom. Translucent markers overlap to show dense areas; zoom in or select an event from the register to inspect it. Multi-country records may have two anchors but count once.

How replay works

The slider uses calendar dates. Playback moves continuously through every calendar day, including quiet days: 8 days per second at 1× (about 30 seconds for the default view), 16 at 2×, and 32 at 4×. Scrubbing snaps to individual dates; the arrow buttons jump to the previous or next event date. New events appear with a small ripple and a quiet musical note. Pitch rises through alerts, recoveries, flights, controlled disposal, military engagement, shoot-downs, crashes, and explosions. Notes use a pentatonic scale, so different types arriving together form a chord. Use the speaker button to mute. Records accumulate up to the selected date. For date ranges and discrepancies, the earliest listed date controls appearance; the full date wording and its basis remain in the details. A discovery or disposal date is not an inferred flight date. Status includes later attribution updates in the supplied snapshot; replay does not reconstruct what was known on each day.

Marker colors

Flight is blue, shot down or armed engagement is purple, crash is amber, and explosion is red. Controlled disposal by authorities, recoveries, and alerts or other unresolved outcomes have separate colors. For records with several stages, the marker prioritizes a reported incident explosion, then a shoot-down or armed engagement, then a crash. The details show the applicable stages. For the 20 August Neptun Deep event, F-16 cannon fire damaged the maritime drone before Navy EOD neutralized it; the map highlights the military engagement, with disposal retained as the subsequent stage. A fire, explosive payload, failed detonation, or nearby explosion alone does not make a record an explosion.

Keep the uncertainty

Colors describe the type of record, not confidence or nationality. Unknown-origin objects, disputed attribution, adjacent EEZ cases and unverified leads retain their stated status. Recovery stages and article updates are not split into extra incidents. The register does not claim exhaustive EU coverage or fresh independent verification of every imported claim.
